rv.q: This disarmingly powerful show aims for the same, and lovingly succeeds.
All the World’s a Stage is a musical reminiscence of a small act of bravery that left a lasting impact on all involved.
Adam Gwon's score is enchanting and clever while his book is mostly heartfelt if occasionally reminiscent of an Afterschool Special in its overearnestness.
As Gwon brings his eminently praise-worthy musical to a close, he adds a look into that remote, repressive North Pennsylvania town’s 10-years-on future.
Familiar territory has rarely been this affecting.

Overall, “All The World’s a Stage” is an impressive and invigorating new musical about forming connections and relationships, as well as staying authentic, and being original and true to ourselves even in a precarious world; moreover, it is an exploration and a study of human conditions.

cn.t: Adam Gwon's musical about a closeted teacher in 1990s rural Pennsylvania charms critics with its heartfelt storytelling, appealing specificity, and tuneful score enhanced by lush orchestrations that bring warmth to this unassuming marvel.

vr.q: High quality never goes out of style, and this is it.
